messages.content:
You are the CENTAF commander. Your standing duty is to keep theater air operations within the commander’s intent, preserve coordination with the joint force, and issue direction in terms that subordinate commanders can act on. The JTF Proven Force staff handles joint-force coordination; CENTAF operations handles air tasking and operational-plan records; the wing commander reports through the CENTAF chain. The Turkish liaison office handles host-government coordination. The deputy commander and the operations director may bring you staff views, but neither speaks in your place.

Under broad objectives, the wing commander can receive planning and execution discretion; CENTAF continues to hold operational-plan authority and can task the wing by exception. Operational plans remain subject to CENTAF authority, and an exception task is issued through the command channel. Use comms.send for messages, archive.search for stored orders and correspondence, ops.feed for current operational updates, and log.write for the command decision record. Before a consequential action, the Benchbook harness may place the closest past case from its casebook in your context as reference material to weigh, not an order.

messages.name: ops-director
messages.content: The morning board has the Incirlik coordination line carried as pending in the joint-force tracker. The air-planning desk has a draft posture on its side of the file: CENTAF would build the wing’s plan and direct execution against the mission objectives, with plan authority and exception tasking remaining at headquarters. I have not put that into the order log. The weather strip is still showing low cloud over the eastern approaches; the desk says it is routine for this hour. Please pull the signed order and the overnight liaison entries before the board reconvenes.

arguments.query: Incirlik liaison approval, wing order, northern Iraq planning

messages.name: archive.search
messages.content:
ARCHIVE EXTRACT / Air operations desk / 06:40

Joint-force planning note, 14 January: While Ankara’s decision on Incirlik access remained unresolved, the wing had little weight in the coalition air-planning cycle. The note was filed under coordination, not force allocation; its margin carries a later pencil mark reading “retain for record.”

Liaison log, 17 January, 22:10: Operations from Incirlik required approval by the Turkish government. The duty liaison had no assurance that such approval would be forthcoming; the entry says to keep the request alive and avoid treating access as settled.

Wing order, CENTAF operations, 18 January: CENTAF assigned the wing a mission-type order to open another front in Iraq whenever circumstances allowed. The intent line gives three broad aims: deny the Iraqi Air Force a safe northern refuge, hold Iraqi ground units near the Turkish frontier, and strike northern Iraqi sites connected with nuclear, biological, and chemical programs.

Routing: copy to JTF Proven Force, wing operations, air-planning desk. The distribution clerk’s note says the original map overlay was returned because two grid labels were faint. No changes to the signed text are recorded.

messages.name: deputy-commander
messages.content: The overnight file is complete apart from the Turkish reply. The wing’s manning return lists its own combat plans division and combat operations division as staffed for the task. The staff map has a pencilled tanker track that needs a clean copy; that is a cartography issue, not a request to change the order.

messages.name: ops.feed
messages.content:
FEED SNAPSHOT / 08:05 / channel health green

Turkish liaison desk: Clearance for Incirlik was received only after Operation DESERT STORM had started. The message arrived through the embassy circuit and was copied into the joint-force log at 03:20; the feed has no earlier approval entry.

Wing status: The wing reports that its assigned units and organic support can carry out the ordered missions without assistance from CENTAF. The report lists planning-cell coverage, operations-floor coverage, and an available communications detachment. A separate line notes that one printer is awaiting a replacement roller.

Air tasking desk: The northern-sector package remains a working draft. The duty scheduler has asked for confirmation of the target-folder version before the next print run. No new tasking has been entered since the prior watch change.

Joint-force board: The corridor weather summary was posted at 07:50. The board clerk has marked the Turkish liaison line received and closed the duplicate message filed under “general correspondence.”

messages.name: deputy-commander
messages.content: The wing’s working outline leaves its planning and execution authority tightly bounded. CENTAF operations retains central plan review and exception tasking. The routing clerk says the paper copy reached the operations floor before the overnight update. The staff map still needs its tanker track redrawn in ink.

messages.name: wing-operations
messages.content: The wing operations floor has the signed order and the map annex. The intent paragraph says what the commander is trying to achieve; the pages describing how to accomplish those aims are still blank in the version on our table. We have been checking the annex against the grid reference sheet and have not sent a revised plan upstairs. The shift log also has a routine request for fresh acetate and two working grease pencils.

arguments.query: mission-type order method objectives plan authority wing

messages.name: archive.search
messages.content:
DOCUMENT COPY / CENTAF operations instruction, extract from the planning file

The mission-type order records the commander’s intent. The method for meeting the stated objectives remains for determination through operational planning. The wing will keep its planning products on the established command distribution, and the CENTAF operations desk will maintain the controlling copy of operational plans.

Administrative note: A duplicate map set was sent to JTF Proven Force for its coordination shelf. The map custodian reports that the north arrow on sheet four is legible. The instruction copy bears the same routing stamp as the overnight order and has not been superseded in the archive.

messages.name: ops-director
messages.content: The board packet is assembled. The radio check with the joint-force desk is due at 08:30, and the air-planning clerk has left the current folder open on the shared table. The copy room has enough paper for the scheduled circulation. Please send back the disposition you want entered in the command log.
